A lithium ion battery (11) that is a test object is housed in a vacuum chamber (14). An initial exhaust pipe (47) and an inspection exhaust pipe (51) are connected to the upper portion of the vacuum chamber (14). The inside of the vacuum chamber (14) is subjected to an initial exhaust through the initial exhaust pipe (47) to lower the pressure inside the vacuum chamber (14) to an inspection pressure (Pe). Thereafter, an inspection exhaust is performed through the inspection exhaust pipe (51). A sensor unit (16) is interposed in the inspection exhaust pipe (51). Exhaust gas passing through the inspection exhaust pipe (51) flows into the sensor unit (16) from an inlet port, and is caused to flow perpendicularly toward the sensor face of a gas sensor by a nozzle provided inside the sensor unit (16). The exhaust gas passes through the inside of the gas sensor, and is discharged to outside of the sensor unit (16) from an exhaust port.

A lithium-ion battery to be tested is placed inside a vacuum chamber so that gas released from the battery can be inspected under controlled pressure conditions. The vacuum chamber is connected to two separate exhaust paths: an initial exhaust pipe and an inspection exhaust pipe.

At the start of the test, the vacuum chamber is evacuated through the initial exhaust pipe. This preliminary evacuation continues until the pressure inside the chamber reaches a predetermined inspection pressure suitable for gas detection. Once the required inspection pressure has been achieved, the exhaust path is switched from the initial exhaust pipe to the inspection exhaust pipe.

Inspection exhaust is then carried out through the inspection exhaust pipe. A sensor unit is installed in this inspection exhaust path to detect gas discharged from the lithium-ion battery. As the exhaust gas flows into the sensor unit, it is guided by a nozzle so that the gas is directed substantially perpendicular to the detection surface of the gas sensor. The gas then passes across or through the sensing region of the gas sensor, enabling the sensor to detect the target gas components. After passing the gas sensor, the exhaust gas is discharged from the sensor unit through an exhaust port.

A lithium-ion battery can be inspected for gas leakage by placing the battery inside a sealed vacuum chamber and reducing the pressure within the chamber. In the initial stage of the inspection, the chamber is evacuated through a first exhaust path, such as an initial exhaust pipe, in order to rapidly lower the internal pressure to a predetermined vacuum level. This preliminary evacuation removes most of the air from the chamber and creates conditions under which gas leaking from the battery, if present, can be drawn out and detected.

After the chamber has reached the required pressure, the exhaust flow used for inspection is routed through a separate inspection exhaust path that includes a sensor unit. The sensor unit is provided with a gas sensor capable of detecting gas components associated with leakage from the lithium-ion battery. During this inspection stage, gas discharged from the vacuum chamber is guided toward the gas sensor in a controlled manner.

In particular, the exhaust gas is directed substantially perpendicularly toward the sensing surface of the gas sensor. The gas then passes through or across the sensor region so that any leaked gas contained in the exhaust stream can be reliably measured. By causing the exhaust gas to impinge directly on the gas sensor, rather than merely flowing past it in an uncontrolled direction, the system improves contact between the leaked gas and the sensing element. This configuration increases detection accuracy and reduces the likelihood that a small amount of leaked gas will be missed.

Accordingly, the inspection apparatus includes a vacuum chamber for receiving the lithium-ion battery, an initial exhaust pipe for reducing the chamber pressure, an inspection exhaust pipe connected to the sensor unit, and a gas sensor positioned so that the exhaust gas flows perpendicularly onto and through the sensor. With this arrangement, leakage from the battery can be detected efficiently and reliably during vacuum inspection.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the following patent embodiment in plain technical language, keeping the reference numerals: a lithium ion battery leak inspection apparatus with a vacuum chamber, initial exhaust pipe, inspection exhaust pipe, and sensor unit.
counterfactuals.output:
A lithium ion battery leak inspection apparatus includes a vacuum chamber that holds a lithium ion battery to be inspected. The chamber is evacuated through two separate exhaust paths: an initial exhaust pipe and an inspection exhaust pipe.

The initial exhaust pipe is used first to quickly reduce the pressure inside the vacuum chamber to a target low-pressure state. After this initial evacuation, the inspection exhaust pipe is used during the actual leak inspection stage.

A sensor unit is connected to the inspection exhaust pipe. While the chamber is under vacuum, if gas or electrolyte vapor leaks from the lithium ion battery, it is drawn through the inspection exhaust pipe and detected by the sensor unit. This allows the apparatus to determine whether the battery has a leak.

In short, the apparatus first evacuates the vacuum chamber through the initial exhaust pipe, then performs leak detection through the inspection exhaust pipe using the sensor unit, improving inspection reliability by separating rapid evacuation from sensitive leak measurement.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise patent-style description of a system for inspecting a lithium ion battery in a vacuum chamber, where exhaust gas is routed through an inspection pipe into a gas sensor via a nozzle.
counterfactuals.output: A battery inspection system includes a vacuum chamber configured to accommodate a lithium ion battery under inspection, an exhaust passage in fluid communication with an interior of the vacuum chamber, an inspection pipe connected to the exhaust passage, and a gas sensor coupled to the inspection pipe through a nozzle. During evacuation or pressure reduction of the vacuum chamber, gas emitted from the lithium ion battery is drawn from the vacuum chamber into the exhaust passage and routed through the inspection pipe. The nozzle directs at least a portion of the routed gas toward a sensing region of the gas sensor, thereby enabling detection of a target gas component indicative of a condition, defect, or failure mode of the lithium ion battery. The inspection pipe and nozzle may be configured to concentrate, accelerate, or regulate the flow of exhaust gas supplied to the gas sensor to improve inspection sensitivity and repeatability.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the operation of a battery gas leak detection apparatus using the component numbers (11), (14), (47), (51), and (16), including initial evacuation and inspection exhaust flow.
counterfactuals.output:
The battery gas leak detection apparatus operates as follows:

A battery **(11)** to be inspected is placed in a sealed inspection chamber or casing **(14)**. Before leak inspection begins, the interior of the chamber **(14)** is initially evacuated so that residual air or background gas is removed. This initial evacuation is carried out through an evacuation/exhaust path connected to the chamber, and the evacuated gas is discharged through the exhaust system **(16)**.

After the initial evacuation, the apparatus switches to the inspection mode. During inspection, gas in the chamber **(14)** is drawn from around the battery **(11)** as an inspection exhaust flow. If gas is leaking from the battery **(11)**, it is entrained in this exhaust flow. The inspection exhaust is guided through the exhaust passage **(51)** to the gas detecting section **(47)**, where the presence or concentration of leaked battery gas is detected. After passing the detector **(47)**, the exhaust gas is discharged through the exhaust outlet/system **(16)**.

Thus, the apparatus first evacuates the chamber **(14)** to establish a clean baseline, then continuously or intermittently draws inspection exhaust from around the battery **(11)** through passage **(51)** past the detector **(47)** and finally out through the exhaust system **(16)**.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract-like paragraph for a patent application about detecting gas from a lithium ion battery housed in a vacuum chamber using an exhaust pipe and sensor unit.
counterfactuals.output: A gas detection system for a lithium ion battery housed within a vacuum chamber is disclosed. The system includes an exhaust pipe in fluid communication with an interior of the vacuum chamber and configured to guide gas discharged from the lithium ion battery toward a sensor unit. The sensor unit is disposed along or coupled to the exhaust pipe and includes one or more gas sensors configured to detect at least one target gas associated with battery abnormality, degradation, leakage, venting, thermal runaway, or electrolyte decomposition. A control unit may receive detection signals from the sensor unit and determine a battery condition based on gas concentration, gas composition, pressure, flow rate, or temporal changes thereof. The system enables early detection of gas generation from the lithium ion battery under vacuum conditions while allowing the generated gas to be collected, transported, and analyzed through the exhaust pipe without exposing the vacuum chamber interior to the external environment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
